title: Integrity and ethical values
desc: Leadership sets and upholds standards of integrity and ethical conduct, and deviations are identified and addressed.

title: Board independence and oversight
desc: A governing body independent of management oversees how internal control is designed and performs.

title: Structure, reporting lines and authority
desc: Management, with oversight, defines organisational structure, reporting lines, authorities and responsibilities.

title: Competent people
desc: The organisation attracts, develops and retains people with the competence needed to meet its objectives.

title: Accountability for control responsibilities
desc: Individuals are held accountable for their internal-control responsibilities.

title: Relevant, quality information
desc: The organisation obtains or produces relevant, reliable information to support internal control.

title: Internal communication
desc: Objectives, responsibilities and control information are communicated internally to those who need them.

title: External communication
desc: The organisation communicates with external parties about matters affecting internal control.

title: Clear objectives
desc: Objectives are specified clearly enough that risks to achieving them can be identified and assessed.

title: Risk identification and analysis
desc: Risks to objectives are identified across the organisation and analysed to decide how to manage them.

title: Fraud risk
desc: The potential for fraud is considered when assessing risks.

title: Changes that affect internal control
desc: Significant internal or external changes that could affect internal control are identified and assessed.

title: Ongoing and separate evaluations
desc: The organisation performs ongoing and/or periodic evaluations to confirm controls are present and working.

title: Communicating control deficiencies
desc: Control deficiencies are evaluated and communicated promptly to those responsible for fixing them, including leadership.

title: Selecting control activities
desc: Control activities are chosen and developed to reduce risks to acceptable levels.

title: General controls over technology
desc: General controls over technology are selected and developed to support objectives.

title: Policies and procedures
desc: Controls are put into practice through policies that set expectations and procedures that implement them.

title: Logical access security
desc: Logical access software, infrastructure and architecture protect information assets from security events.

title: User registration and authorisation
desc: New users are registered and authorised before credentials are issued; credentials are removed when no longer needed.

title: Role-based access changes
desc: Access is granted, changed or removed based on roles and responsibilities, applying least privilege and segregation of duties.

title: Physical access
desc: Physical access to facilities and sensitive locations (data centres, backup media) is restricted to authorised people.

title: Secure disposal of assets
desc: Protections over physical assets are only removed once data on them can no longer be read or recovered.

title: Protection against external threats
desc: Logical access measures protect against threats from outside the system boundary.

title: Protecting data in transmission and movement
desc: Transmission, movement and removal of information is limited to authorised parties and protected.

title: Malicious and unauthorised software
desc: Controls prevent or detect, and respond to, malicious or unauthorised software.

title: Detecting vulnerabilities and configuration drift
desc: Detection and monitoring identify configuration changes that introduce vulnerabilities and newly discovered vulnerabilities.

title: Monitoring for anomalies
desc: System components are monitored for anomalies indicating attacks, disasters or errors, and anomalies are analysed.

title: Evaluating security events
desc: Security events are evaluated to decide whether they are incidents, and action is taken to prevent or address failures.

title: Incident response
desc: Identified incidents are handled through a defined response programme to contain, remediate and communicate.

title: Recovery from incidents
desc: Activities to recover from identified incidents are identified, developed and carried out.

title: Controlled changes
desc: Changes to infrastructure, data, software and procedures are authorised, designed, tested, approved and documented.

title: Business disruption risks
desc: Risk-mitigation activities are identified and developed for potential business disruptions.

title: Vendor and partner risk
desc: Risks from vendors and business partners are assessed and managed.

title: Capacity management
desc: Current processing capacity and usage are maintained, monitored and evaluated so capacity can meet demand and objectives.

title: Environmental protection, backup and recovery infrastructure
desc: Environmental protections, software, backup processes and recovery infrastructure are put in place and maintained.

title: Recovery plan testing
desc: Recovery plan procedures that support system recovery are tested.

title: Identifying and protecting confidential information
desc: Confidential information is identified and maintained in line with confidentiality commitments.

title: Disposing of confidential information
desc: Confidential information is disposed of in line with confidentiality commitments.

title: Processing specifications
desc: Relevant information about processing objectives - data definitions and product/service specifications - is produced and communicated.

title: Input completeness and accuracy
desc: Policies and procedures over system inputs ensure completeness and accuracy.

title: Processing controls
desc: Policies and procedures over system processing produce outputs that meet objectives.

title: Output completeness, accuracy and timeliness
desc: Outputs are made available or delivered completely, accurately and on time, as specified.

title: Storage of inputs, in-process items and outputs
desc: Inputs, items in processing and outputs are stored completely, accurately and on time, as specified.

title: Privacy notice
desc: Data subjects receive notice of the organisation's privacy practices, updated and communicated promptly when practices change.

title: Choice and consent
desc: Data subjects are told their choices about collection, use, retention, disclosure and disposal of personal data, and consent is obtained where required.

title: Collection limited to purpose
desc: Personal information is collected only in line with privacy objectives.

title: Explicit consent where required
desc: Where explicit consent is needed, its necessity and consequences are explained and consent is obtained before collection.

title: Use limited to purpose
desc: Use of personal information is limited to the purposes identified in privacy objectives.

title: Retention
desc: Personal information is retained only as long as privacy objectives allow.

title: Secure disposal of personal information
desc: Personal information is disposed of securely.

title: Access by data subjects
desc: Identified and authenticated data subjects can review their personal information and obtain a copy on request.

title: Correction and amendment
desc: Personal information is corrected or amended based on data-subject input, and changes are passed to third parties where committed.

title: Disclosure to third parties with consent
desc: Personal information is disclosed to third parties only with the data subject's explicit prior consent where required.

title: Record of authorised disclosures
desc: A complete, accurate and timely record of authorised disclosures is kept.

title: Record of unauthorised disclosures
desc: A complete, accurate and timely record of detected or reported unauthorised disclosures, including breaches, is kept.

title: Privacy commitments from vendors
desc: Vendors and third parties with access to personal information commit to privacy obligations and are periodically assessed.

title: Vendor breach notification
desc: Vendors and third parties commit to notify the organisation of actual or suspected unauthorised disclosures.

title: Breach notification
desc: Breaches and incidents are notified to affected data subjects, regulators and others as required.

title: Accounting of disclosures
desc: When a data subject asks, the organisation tells them what personal data it holds about them and to whom that data has been disclosed.

title: Data quality
desc: Personal information is kept accurate, up to date, complete and relevant.

title: Inquiries, complaints and disputes
desc: There is a process to receive, address, resolve and communicate the resolution of privacy inquiries, complaints and disputes, and compliance is monitored.
